message:
docs(history): three explanations for the capture failure, none of them reproduced

The latest was that the failing runs measured a Debug binary against an fps
threshold. Six runs say otherwise: three Debug and three Release, all passing,
with Debug marginally the faster of the two. Config cannot turn 42.99 into 59.33.

That is the third proposed cause after live-host contention and "unexplained", and
none of the three reproduced here. What does survive every run, on both machines
and both configs, is that 1/copyAvg matches the measured fps to the decimal --
copy time is the ceiling -- and that the copy ranges from 16.8 to 23.3 ms. The 50
fps threshold is exactly 20.0 ms, which puts it in the middle of the observed
spread. So the verdict is set by load at that moment, and the load behind the
failing runs can no longer be reconstructed.

Both of us reached three times for an explanation that was plausible and
unverified. An explanation that does not reproduce is not an explanation.

Separately, udp_control_e2e: reported as a Release failure, but Debug fails
identically -- 1 pass, 17 failures, three runs in a row -- while the same Debug
binary passed with 18 a few hours earlier. It dies at udp hello ack failed, so
the session never forms and the other seventeen are consequences. It is state on
this machine, not configuration; a UDP port already in use is a candidate and is
not claimed. Nothing in the three commits touches it.

The totals now have three reproduction conditions rather than one: suite output
format, config (Debug 1820, Release 1803), and build freshness. The per-suite
files carry config and build time in their header.

Also on the list: suites leave processes behind. Two survived a sweep and blocked
a Release link with LNK1104.
